headline: Day-Use Permits and Bivouac Regulations in the High Desert
reservation: A day-use parking permit is required and must be displayed on your vehicle; these are available at automated fee stations within the park. The Bivy Campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis and does not accept advance reservations. Check the official Oregon State Parks website for seasonal raptor nesting closures that may restrict access to specific rock faces.

days.title: Volcanic Spires and River Loops

stops.name: Misery Ridge Trail
stops.detail: Complete the steep ascent early to view the Monkey Face spire and the Cascade Range.

stops.name: River Trail
stops.detail: Follow the Crooked River at the base of the cliffs for a level return walk and wildlife spotting.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for local transit; conditions vary
days.note: Misery Ridge is exposed; ensure adequate hydration for the steep switchbacks.

days.title: Canyon Rims and Higher Vantage Points

stops.name: Summit Trail
stops.detail: Take a longer, gradual climb to the park's northern heights for expansive desert views.

stops.name: Burma Road
stops.detail: Hike this historic route to reach the highest overlooks above the basalt gorge.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for transit; conditions vary
days.note: Trail surfaces are composed of loose volcanic soil; traction varies by weather.

days.title: Geological Wonders and Nearby Chasms

stops.name: Wolf Tree Trail
stops.detail: Explore the upstream river environment away from the main climbing walls for solitude.

stops.name: Peter Skene Ogden State Scenic Viewpoint
stops.detail: Drive a short distance to view the dramatic bridge crossings over the Crooked River canyon.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for the regional circuit; conditions vary
days.note: The scenic viewpoint is a separate park unit; check for separate fee requirements.

intel.title: Morning Arrival
intel.text: Main parking lots frequently reach capacity by 10 AM during spring and fall weekends. Arrive at sunrise to secure a spot near the welcome center.

intel.title: High Desert Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable at the rim but can be completely lost within the canyon depths. Verify your route at the trailhead maps before descending.

intel.title: Terrebonne Services
intel.text: Fuel and basic supplies are located in Terrebonne and Redmond. No fuel or food services are available once you enter the park boundaries.

intel.title: Raptor Nesting
intel.text: Specific cliffs are closed to all use from late winter through summer to protect nesting eagles and falcons. Consult the official closure map at the park entry.

intel.title: Bivy Campground
intel.text: The walk-in bivy area is for tent camping only; sleeping in vehicles is prohibited in parking lots. Verify the seasonal opening dates for the campground showers.

plan.arrival: Fly into Roberts Field (RDM) in Redmond, a 20-minute drive from the park, and secure supplies in Redmond or Terrebonne before check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved access roads; check for specific height clearances if bringing an RV to the Bivy parking area.
plan.goldenHour: The park overlooks near the main entrance for sunset, as the tuff walls glow orange; seasonal times vary.
